title: Medal of Honor
subtitle: "It is from the giver that honor derives, not the receiver."

items.text: Front Desk, Tuesday's Motel
The maid stands behind the front desk in the motel lobby. She's checking in her new guests.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: That'll be 25 dollars altogether. Will that be on card or cash?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Cash, please.
The maid holds up the passport, comparing the information on it.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hey, do you know if there's an armament factory in the town nearby?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: An armament factory?
She studies Lilya's outfit and smiles as she responds.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Yes, there is one. Would you like a map?
She opens a drawer, pulls out a map, and hands it to her.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: If you plan on visiting, make sure to return early. It can be a difficult walk in the dark.
Lilya quickly finds the town labeled "Chisos" on the map.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Doesn't seem far from here.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: It's about an hour's walk. I'd recommend leaving tomorrow morning.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: It's getting late. It's best not to be outside at night.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Thanks, but I'm going right now.
She moves with swift purpose to the front door.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Nothing can go wrong as long as I have the Red 38 by my side.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Call me if anything happens.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Like what? I can handle myself.
A rush of wind enters as Lilya opens the door and makes her way out of the motel.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Don't worry. She'll check in later.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Here's your passport.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Have you been working here since the opening of this place?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How's business?
The maid laughs softly.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Not too great. It's the off-season now.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: You don't seem too good at small talk. Is there anything you'd like to ask?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I do have one question.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Have you seen a sheep-headed arcanist around?
She shows the information provided by the Foundation.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ah, that's not a face you'd easily forget.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: And why are you looking for this arcanist?
For world peace.

branch.text: The maid blinks in surprise, then laughs.

branch.speaker: Tuesday
branch.text: Well, that makes this request simply too adorable to turn down.

items.text: Looking for an editor of UTTU.

branch.speaker: Tuesday
branch.text: UTTU ... I think I've heard of that before.

branch.speaker: Tuesday
branch.text: That's a magazine specially made for arcanists, right?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Well, I'm sorry to say that I've never met an arcanist with the head of a sheep.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I can help you ask around if you—
Suddenly, the ceiling starts to tremble.
A surge of arcane energy comes from above.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's ...

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Sounds like something's gone wrong upstairs. Sorry about that.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Let's head up. Your room's on the second floor, too. Then we can take a look at what's happened.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sounds good.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Just so you know, the guests upstairs are a little ...
The maid hesitates.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Well, you can stay behind me if you like.
Hallway, Tuesday's Motel

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: How about it?
A voice echoes from down the hall.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: It's just a simple room swap. I'm sure it won't be no trouble at all for a generous lady such as yourself.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: That's the guest staying in room 210. She arrived here the night before yesterday.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: She was injured when she came in. Seems it didn't take her long to recover.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But I don't quite understand why she insists on swapping rooms with the other guests. If she does the same to you, please call the front desk. I'll do my best to help.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why don't you offer her your help? She needs it more than I do.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, things don't work like that here, Miss.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Everyone has their own secrets. With the variety of guests we get, it's best to keep your mouth shut, or else somebody will shut it for you.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Although there are fewer bounty hunters around these days, my advice is to stay quiet if you don't want any trouble.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Especially if you're dealing with an armed mercenary. You know how things like that play out down here in Texas, don't you?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Understood.
The voice down the hall continues.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Or do you have something else in mind?

items.speaker: Female Guest
items.text: Is your room bigger and better than this one?
A more lively voice chimes in.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: That's the guest of room 218 speaking. She too is a young lady like you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You remember all the guests and their room numbers?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: You'd remember her too if she'd been staying in your motel for a month. Ms. Kimberly's been here for just over that.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Hm?
The maid quickly moves toward the source of the voice.
The man before her looks haggard, his back slightly hunched, his eyes yellowed and cloudy.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Mirror ... The mirror ...

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Mr. Stefen, are you coming out for some fresh air?
Everyone in the hallway turns to look at the maid.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Maid! You're just in time.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I'd like to swap rooms with this Kimberly lady.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: If Ms. Kimberly and yourself have come to an agreement, then I see no reason why you can't do so.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Ah.
The man makes a dry, rasping sound, his vocal cords trembling unnaturally. It's like he's speaking for the first time in his life.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Have we met?
This response seems to trigger something. His expression twists.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Vertin?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's me. Do I know you, sir?

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: I saw you—in the newspaper.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Arh, the newspaper, that vacuum bomb—did you see the explosion? You must have, because you made it happen! You dropped the bomb! You murderers!

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: But have any of you been brought to justice? No, not a single one! Instead, you were congratulated and given medals.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Revolting! Disgusting! Why were you rewarded for murder?!
He blabbers on, working himself into a frenzy.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Meanwhile, I'm stuck in this hotel. Lord, is this what my life has come to?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But we've never met before. I don't even know your name, sir.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Of course you don't know me. But I'll get the truth out. I'll expose your crimes to the public!
The man's deranged rant continues, his knuckles turning white as he clenches his fists.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: That rotting woman in the tub, that sheep-headed monster, and that one inside the mirror.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sheep-headed, you say?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Wait! Sir—

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Shh. Don't startle him. He's totally crazy.

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: I should've known it was all fake!

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: If they're giving out medals for killing people ...

items.speaker: Stefen
items.text: Ah, then I should have one, too. That shiny medal—it should be mine!
He bites down hard on his lip, his cloudy eyes staring straight ahead.
He steps forward.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Stay back!
But the man has already lunged at them.
A single blow from the butt of the mercenary's shotgun knocks the man out.
The maid breathes heavily, her face slightly flushed.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I'm ever so sorry about all this, Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: You've only just arrived, and you've had to deal with so much trouble already.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Oh, it's no trouble. In fact, I'm glad that we came here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That man said he'd seen a "sheep-headed monster."

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, that ... He's quite delusional. Surely you won't take the ramblings of a madman for a fact, will you?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: He's been peculiar since the day he checked in. He spasms and twitches and pays little attention to his surroundings.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: It's best not to have a face-to-face conversation with him. Who knows what he'll do next.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Hey, you, maid! Enough chatter. You have a job to do.
The girl impatiently interrupts their conversation.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I've accepted the offer this, uh, Ms. Argus made. What's next? What should we do?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Apologies, Ms. Kimberly. I'll be with you in a moment.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Could the both of you wait for me at the front desk? The rooms need a tidy-up before they can be occupied. You may take a rest on the couch in the lobby while you wait.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ms. Vertin, I'm afraid I'll have to leave you here. Do you mind going to your room alone?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not at all.
The suitcase sways with her steps as she heads to her room.
Once again, the air pulses with the flow of arcane energy, compelling her to look back.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Ma'am, you can just leave the room as it is. If you clean it, it'll interfere with my work.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: You might wanna check on that Kimberly lady. She looks starved. She wouldn't stop shaking.
A cluster of emerald light sparks in the mercenary's left eye, scattering like a bird unfurling its brilliant tail feathers.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, Ms. Kimberly. Would you like something to eat?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I'm fine!
The guest's face visibly sours.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I agreed to change rooms, didn't I? Why are you two still mocking me?
She turns her attention to the mercenary.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: You're not exactly a pleasant person to do business with; you know that, right?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Well, darn, what got you so riled up?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: It's too late now. A deal's a deal. You can backpedal if you like, but it ain't wise to mess with a girl packing heat down here in Texas.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Later, Ms. Kimberly.
The mercenary's eye gleams as she turns the lock and enters her hard-won room.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Her arcane skill.
